harlech_guide.text: Welcome to Harlech Castle. Edward I built it between 1283 and 1289 on a cliff, with walls meant to be unbeatable.
It once had a water gate so ships could reach it from the sea. The sea has since backed away and left the castle to enjoy the view.
In the Wars of the Roses it held out for seven years, the longest siege in British history. The song Men of Harlech is said to remember it.

harlech_harpist.text: I play Men of Harlech all day. It is the only tune the walls like. The rest, they have heard before.

then.text: The copied page is on the wall by the fire. The visitors read Branwen now, and then they look out at Ireland and go quiet. Diolch.
There are four branches: Pwyll, Branwen, Manawydan and Math. The third one is about a plague of mice, and I am not making that up.
You have it! A page of the White Book, in a copy, with the starling in the margin. Branwen's letter went from Ireland to Harlech; yours came the other way and took less time.

A cyfarwydd is a storyteller, and a storyteller pays in stories. Here is the Mabinogion to keep, and bara brith for the road. Gwlad beirdd a chantorion: a land of poets and singers. You are one of us now, whether you like it or not.
Now fly, starling. The scholar at the National Library in Aberystwyth, down the coast, will copy the page for us. Tell them Harlech sent you.

else.text: Read the board by the wall first, the one about Branwen. A messenger should know the message.
{greeting} Shwmae. I am the cyfarwydd here, the storyteller, and this is where the second branch of the Mabinogi begins: Bendigeidfran on this rock, looking out to Ireland.
Branwen, his sister, was married off to the king of Ireland and badly treated. She taught a starling to speak, tied a letter to its wing and sent it home to Harlech. The oldest airmail in Wales.

I want a page of the real thing on the wall: the White Book of Rhydderch, from about 1350, at the National Library in Aberystwyth. Read Branwen's board here, then go south and ask the scholar there for a copy. You will be my starling.
